grammar.title: Name the source of a report
grammar.formation: Noun naming a source + によると/によれば. A verb clause can use 聞いたところによると. The polite reporting variant is によりますと.
grammar.explanation: The phrase identifies whose information is being reported. A source may be a statement, an article or a person’s account. The following proposition can use reported そうだ or という, or state the information directly in news writing. It does not turn a forecast into an event that has already happened. Retrieve earlier reporting language and distinguish the information-source use from causal によって.
grammar.example: 続報によると、バスは九時に運行を始めた。
grammar.translation: According to the follow-up report, the bus began operating at nine.

examples.ja: {続報|ぞくほう}によると、バスは{九時|くじ}に{運行|うんこう}を{始|はじ}めた。
examples.en: According to the follow-up report, the bus began operating at nine.

examples.ja: {担当|たんとう}{者|しゃ}の{話|はなし}によれば、{復旧|ふっきゅう}にはまだ{時間|じかん}がかかるそうだ。
examples.en: According to the person in charge, repairs will still take time.

examples.ja: {聞|き}いたところによると、{説明|せつめい}{会|かい}は{午後|ごご}に{変|か}わったという。
examples.en: From what I’ve heard, the briefing has moved to the afternoon.

grammar.mistake: Use a source noun directly before によると, not 新聞がによると. によると and によれば are both valid here; do not reject one to force the other.

grammar.title: Read a reported assessment
grammar.formation: Plain proposition + とみられる/とみられている. A complete noun/な-adjective predicate uses だ, as in 原因は故障だとみられる. Attributive noun labels may omit だ. Active: Xは…とみている.
grammar.explanation: News writing uses とみられる for an assessment, inference or expectation. The article may state a basis or name an assessor. It is different from reporting a confirmed reopening. とみている names someone’s assessment actively. In a casual response, say みたい or と思う rather than making every line sound like a report. The text and surrounding attribution determine whose view it is; the form alone does not mean everyone agrees.
grammar.example: 電車は明日の午前に再開するとみられる。
grammar.translation: The trains are expected to resume tomorrow morning.

examples.ja: {電車|でんしゃ}は{明日|あした}の{午前|ごぜん}に{再開|さいかい}するとみられる。

examples.ja: {不通|ふつう}の{原因|げんいん}は{線路|せんろ}の{被害|ひがい}だとみられる。

examples.ja: {事業|じぎょう}{者|しゃ}は{復旧|ふっきゅう}に{二日|ふつか}かかるとみている。

grammar.mistake: Do not read 再開するとみられる as すでに再開した: expected resumption is not completed resumption. Do not combine a polite predicate 再開します directly with とみられる.

grammar.title: Find the event and the response
grammar.formation: Noun/event noun phrase + を受けて/を受け、 + subsequent response. A whole proposition can be nominalised with こと: 利用者が増えたことを受けて.
grammar.explanation: This formal news connector presents an event, request or result followed by a response or reaction. In this unit, requests lead to a timetable decision. Written を受け is the connective form. It is not merely the receipt of a package; receiving an item normally uses 受け取る. In a conversation the friends quote the article, then explain what the change means for their own journey.
grammar.example: 利用者からの要望を受けて、夜間のバスを増便する。
grammar.translation: In response to requests from users, the operator will add nighttime buses.

examples.ja: {利用|りよう}{者|しゃ}からの{要望|ようぼう}を{受|う}けて、{夜間|やかん}のバスを{増便|ぞうびん}する。
examples.en: In response to requests from users, the operator will add nighttime buses.

examples.ja: {調査|ちょうさ}{結果|けっか}を{受|う}け、{市|し}は{計画|けいかく}を{見直|みなお}した。
examples.en: In response to the survey results, the city revised its plan.

examples.ja: {利用|りよう}{者|しゃ}が{増|ふ}えたことを{受|う}けて、{窓口|まどぐち}を{増設|ぞうせつ}した。
examples.en: Following an increase in users, more service counters were installed.

grammar.mistake: Nominalise a verb proposition before を: 増えたことを受けて, not 増えたを受けて. Several cause/basis connectors can fit real contexts; form tasks explicitly request this connector.

grammar.title: Read the change that accompanies another change
grammar.formation: Noun or dictionary verb (+ の) + に伴って/に伴い. Before a noun use に伴う + noun. Written に伴い is connective, not a noun modifier.
grammar.explanation: One development brings or goes with another development: a relocation and a new route, or growing use and longer waits. This can describe gradual changes or a single event; it is not limited to two quantities increasing at the same rate. It does not itself establish a measured cause. Distinguish に伴い followed by a clause from に伴う followed by a noun.
grammar.example: 図書館の移転に伴い、バスの経路を変えた。
grammar.translation: Along with the library’s relocation, the bus route was changed.

examples.ja: {図書館|としょかん}の{移転|いてん}に{伴|ともな}い、バスの{経路|けいろ}を{変|か}えた。

examples.ja: {利用|りよう}{者|しゃ}が{増|ふ}えるに{伴|ともな}って、{窓口|まどぐち}で{待|ま}つ{時間|じかん}も{長|なが}くなった。
examples.en: As the number of users grew, waits at the counter also became longer.

examples.ja: {改正|かいせい}に{伴|ともな}う{変更|へんこう}{点|てん}を{案内|あんない}する。
examples.en: Explain the changes accompanying the timetable revision.

grammar.mistake: Use 改正に伴う変更 before a noun, not 改正に伴い変更. A response to requests and a change accompanying relocation are different relationships, even when other connectors overlap.

dialogues.title: The interview is across the closed section
dialogues.scene: Yui has an interview near North Station at one today. She calls Bao to ask about the rail interruption. They read the nine-thirty update and work out a bus journey.

dialogues.title: Can we take the bus after closing?
dialogues.scene: Ren and Yui read a local report during a break at the café. The library has recently moved near East Station a month ago. An announced evening-bus trial starts next month; they check the weekdays, last bus and café closing time.

readings.title: Three extra evening buses for a trial
paragraphs: {市|し}とバスの{事業|じぎょう}{者|しゃ}は、{来月|らいげつ}{一日|ついたち}から{東|ひがし}{駅|えき}と{図書館|としょかん}を{結|むす}ぶ{路線|ろせん}の{夜間|やかん}{運行|うんこう}を{拡充|かくじゅう}する。{利用|りよう}{者|しゃ}からの{要望|ようぼう}を{受|う}けて、{平日|へいじつ}の{最終|さいしゅう}{便|びん}を{午後|ごご}{八時|はちじ}から{九時|くじ}{半|はん}へ{変|か}える。{八時|はちじ}{半|はん}、{九時|くじ}、{九時|くじ}{半|はん}の{三便|さんびん}を{追加|ついか}し、{三|さん}か{月|げつ}{間|かん}{試験|しけん}{的|てき}に{運行|うんこう}する。

{図書館|としょかん}は{先月|せんげつ}、{駅|えき}の{近|ちか}くに{移転|いてん}した。{移転|いてん}に{伴|ともな}い、{夕方|ゆうがた}のバス{利用|りよう}が{増|ふ}えている。{市|し}は{沿線|えんせん}の{利用|りよう}{者|しゃ}にアンケートを{行|おこな}い、{三百十二人|さんびゃくじゅうににん}から{回答|かいとう}を{得|え}た。うち{百八十四人|ひゃくはちじゅうよにん}が、{夜|よる}の{便|びん}を{増|ふ}やしてほしいと{答|こた}えた。

{増便|ぞうびん}に{伴|ともな}う{経費|けいひ}の{一部|いちぶ}は{市|し}が{負担|ふたん}する。{当面|とうめん}、{料金|りょうきん}の{値上|ねあ}げは{行|おこな}わない。{昼間|ひるま}の{便|びん}と{土日|どにち}の{時刻|じこく}{表|ひょう}は{変|か}わらない。{図書館|としょかん}の{閉館|へいかん}{時刻|じこく}も{今|いま}のままだ。{乗|の}り{場|ば}の{位置|いち}は{変|か}えず、{駅前|えきまえ}の{掲示|けいじ}にも{新|あたら}しい{便|びん}を{載|の}せる。

{事業|じぎょう}{者|しゃ}は{試験|しけん}{期間|きかん}{中|ちゅう}に、{便|びん}ごとの{利用|りよう}{者|しゃ}{数|すう}と{遅|おく}れを{記録|きろく}する。{今後|こんご}の{運行|うんこう}は、その{結果|けっか}を{見|み}て{決|き}めるため、{夜間|やかん}の{増便|ぞうびん}を{恒久|こうきゅう}{的|てき}に{続|つづ}けるかどうかはまだ{決|き}まっていない。{新|あたら}しい{時刻|じこく}{表|ひょう}は{今月|こんげつ}{二十五日|にじゅうごにち}に{駅|えき}と{市|し}のサイトで{公表|こうひょう}する。{市|し}は{利用|りよう}の{推移|すいい}を{調|しら}べ、{沿線|えんせん}の{声|こえ}も{聞|き}く{予定|よてい}だ。

exercises.prompt: Why does Yui need a way to North Station today?
options: She has a one o’clock interview nearby
She has an interview there tomorrow morning
She works as a railway repairer
exercises.explain: Yui says 今日一時の面接, near North Station.

exercises.prompt: Which transport is reported to have already started?
options: The replacement bus, at nine today
The interrupted trains, at nine today
A new night bus starting next month
exercises.explain: Bao reads 九時から出てる about the bus; tomorrow morning is the forecast for the trains.

exercises.prompt: What departure does Yui tentatively choose?
options: Eleven-thirty by bus
One o’clock by train
Seven in the evening by bus
exercises.explain: じゃ、十一時半に出ようかな is a tentative plan, with extra time for possible crowds.

exercises.context: Form practice: identify the company update as the information source using によると.
exercises.line: {会社|かいしゃ}の{続報|ぞくほう}＿＿、{電車|でんしゃ}はまだ{止|と}まっている。
options: によると
がによると
なによると
exercises.explain: A source noun phrase attaches directly to によると.

exercises.context: Form practice: quote the complete noun proposition “resumption is tomorrow morning” with とみられる.
options: {明日|あした}の{午前|ごぜん}だとみられる
{明日|あした}の{午前|ごぜん}なとみられる
{明日|あした}の{午前|ごぜん}にとみられる
exercises.explain: The complete noun predicate 明日の午前だ is quoted with と. This sentence states an assessment, not that trains are already running.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Bao after hearing the forecast. You still need to travel today; choose the response that fits the update.
exercises.line: 「{明日|あした}の{午前|ごぜん}に{再開|さいかい}するとみられる」だって。
options: じゃ、{今日|きょう}はバスで{行|い}くね。
じゃ、もう{電車|でんしゃ}が{動|うご}いてるんだね。
じゃ、{今日|きょう}の{面接|めんせつ}も{来月|らいげつ}だね。
exercises.explain: The forecast is for tomorrow; taking the bus fits today’s interview. Nothing changes the interview date.
The source phrase precedes the proposition; とみられる follows plain 再開する. This is one authored order, not unrestricted writing.
tiles: {明日|あした}の{午前|ごぜん}に
exercises.meaning: Constrained form practice: place the source first, then say the trains are expected to resume tomorrow morning.

exercises.prompt: Which section is still running normally in the nine-thirty update?
options: The section south of East Station
The whole section between East and North Stations
Every section north of North Station
exercises.explain: The first paragraph explicitly says 東駅より南の区間 is normal; the East–North section is closed.

exercises.prompt: What condition must be met for the expected tomorrow-morning reopening?
options: Inspection after the water recedes must find no major damage
Everyone must cancel today’s interviews
All passengers must buy a new bus pass
exercises.explain: The second paragraph gives the condition 大きな損傷が見つからなければ. The exact time will be announced later.

exercises.prompt: Which bus detail is explicitly stated?
options: The fare matches the train fare for that section and commuter passes are valid
The fare is free for every passenger
The bus runs directly with no intermediate stops
exercises.explain: The third paragraph states equal fares and valid passes, plus two intermediate stops.

exercises.prompt: When will the later last bus apply?
options: Weekdays from next month
Every day starting tonight
Weekends only from tomorrow
exercises.explain: Ren says 来月から and 平日だけ; Yui confirms weekends stay unchanged.

exercises.prompt: How long is the initial trial?
options: Three months
Three days
One year
exercises.explain: Ren says とりあえず三か月、やってみる.

exercises.prompt: Why is catching the last bus still conditional for the café staff?
options: They close at nine and need to finish cleaning up quickly
The bus starts before the café opens
The café is already permanently closed
exercises.explain: Ren says 片付けが早く終われば間に合いそう. The last bus is nine-thirty.

exercises.context: Form practice: nominalise the stated increase in users before を受けて.
exercises.line: {利用|りよう}{者|しゃ}が{増|ふ}えた＿＿、{夜間|やかん}の{便|びん}を{増|ふ}やした。
options: ことを{受|う}けて
を{受|う}けて
ことが{受|う}けて
exercises.explain: The preceding verb proposition needs こと before を受けて. The later clause states the response.

exercises.context: Form practice: modify 変更点 with に伴う after 改正.
exercises.line: {改正|かいせい}＿＿{変更|へんこう}{点|てん}を{案内|あんない}する。
options: に{伴|ともな}う
に{伴|ともな}い
な{伴|ともな}う
exercises.explain: Use the noun-modifying form に伴う directly before 変更点. に伴い introduces a following clause.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Ren. You want to confirm how the weekday trial affects a Sunday journey.
exercises.line: {平日|へいじつ}だけだけど、{最終|さいしゅう}が{九時|くじ}{半|はん}になるみたい。
options: じゃ、{日曜|にちよう}の{帰|かえ}りは{今|いま}の{時刻|じこく}{表|ひょう}で{考|かんが}えるね。
じゃ、{日曜|にちよう}も{九時|くじ}{半|はん}まで{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}だね。
じゃ、{今日|きょう}から{全|すべ}てのバスが{無料|むりょう}なんだね。
exercises.explain: The change applies to weekdays from next month. Weekends retain the current timetable.
に伴う modifies the noun phrase 利用の変化. This is one authored order.
tiles: {利用|りよう}の{変化|へんか}を
exercises.meaning: Constrained form practice: say they investigated the changes in use accompanying the relocation. Put the relocation modifier first.

exercises.prompt: What do the figures 312 and 184 describe?
options: 312 questionnaire respondents; 184 wanted more night buses
312 new buses; 184 new stations
312 households surveyed; 184 buses cancelled
exercises.explain: The second paragraph explicitly names respondents as people, then says 184 requested more nighttime services.

exercises.prompt: Which detail remains unchanged in the trial?
options: Daytime services, weekend timetables and the library’s closing time
The weekday last bus at eight
The total number of weekday night buses
exercises.explain: The third paragraph lists the unchanged daytime, weekend and library-closing arrangements. Three night buses are added.

exercises.prompt: What will determine the service after the trial?
options: Recorded use and delays during the trial, with further user feedback
An already-made decision to keep it permanently
A promised fare rise on the first day
exercises.explain: The last paragraph says the operator will record use and delays and decide from the results. Permanent continuation is not decided.

recycling.reason: The friends need a route to an interview and a later bus after a café shift. Only recent words that naturally occur in these practical conversations and readings are counted; unrelated opinion and notice vocabulary is not inserted to reach a quota.

grammar: accompanying change に伴い/に伴う
watch.prompt: Optionally use your own news text or recording. Identify who supplies the information, one stated event, one prediction, and any condition or time attached to it. Notice how people paraphrase the report in everyday speech. Save useful lines in context.
